page.layout: One column of running text, with a running head at the top and a catchword at the lower right. No marginal notes on this page. The partial page at the far right belongs to the neighbouring opening and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: Laodiceæ: idcirco cap. 4. vult Apostolus hanc epistolam Colossensibus communem esse cum Laodicensibus. Hanc Plinius lib. 5. cap. 32. inter celeberrimas Phrygiæ ciuitates numerat, & eius quoque meminit Herodotus, lib. 7. & Strabo lib. 12. Etsi autem ibi non docuerat Apostolus; cùm tamen apud eos per prædicationem Euangelij Ecclesia collecta esset, de eius statu certior factus, (cap. 2. v. 5.) procul dubio per Epaphram illius Ecclesiæ ministrum, qui S. Paulo Romæ aderat, dum hæc scriberet, noluit Apostolus Gentium committere, quin eos etiam de nonnullis necessariis commonefaceret.

Occasio igitur hæc fuisse videtur, quòd intellexerat Apostolus, fermenti aliquid Pharisaici & humanarum traditionum à nonnullis admisceri doctrinæ Euangelij, quorum alij nimis Judaizantes, ritus & ceremonias Legis urgebant: alij ex gentibus conversi, nescio quæ philosophica dogmata, subtilia potius quàm utilia, invehebant: quibus nimis remisse occurrebatur, saltem à pastore illius loci, Archippo, cuius segnities notari videtur cap. 4.

Hoc autem ordine in hac epistola progreditur Apostolus, ut ante omnia revocet eos ad doctrinam ipsis fideliter ab Epaphra traditam, & inprimis ad fundamentum & caput Ecclesiæ, Christum, & ad revelationem ingentis illius mysterij & beneficiorum Christi, in quo omnes salutis[?] nostræ partes sitas esse, luculenter docet Apostolus cap.1. ut merito immotum & incon-cussum manere debeat illud fundamentum, verf.23. Capite secundo, infert ex precedenti

page.notes: The right-hand partial page belongs to the adjacent opening and was left out. The word "salutis" in the penultimate paragraph is read with doubt, because the long s is hard to separate from f in this print. The reading "revelationem" was chosen for the word printed in the scan as "reuelationem"; the exact spelling is uncertain. The catchword "doctrina," stands alone at the lower right and is taken as the catchword.
